steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet.
Combine confectioner's sugar, evaporated milk, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract in a small bowl.

Beat butter and white sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth. Mix in egg and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a small bowl. Gradually add flour mixture to creamed mixture, mixing well. Roll dough into 1-inch balls and place on prepared baking sheet; make an indentation with finger in center of each cookie.

Bake in preheated oven for 10 minutes. Fill depressions with jam and continue to bake until lightly browned, 10 to 15 minutes longer. Cool for 2 minutes, then remove to wire racks. Drizzle confectioner's sugar glaze mixture over warm cookies; cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Raspberry Ribbons
raw_recipe.description: Beautiful, buttery cookies are filled with raspberry jam and glazed to look like ribbons.

review.reviewBody: These were tasty! Not sure where they got their name, as they look nothing like ribbons, but still a good cookie. Subbed blackberry jam because of a friend's preference, but I think they would have been even better with raspberry preserves. I had to add an additional Tbsp of evaporated milk to the glaze to make it thin enough to drizzle. I think this would be an excellent recipe adapted with lemon flavoring in the cookie and blueberry preserves for the filling!
These are fantastic! My dad requests them every Father's Day and Christmas. I always add a splash of almond flavoring for a little something extra.

I had eaten these cookies at a recent holiday cookie exchange I attended and they were delicious! I had no idea who made them so when I came home I went on this site and found this recipe, made them and they were exactly what I had eaten. Made the recipe as written and I love them! Will add them to my Christmas baking list!
These came out delicious! I used raspberry apricot jam, so good!

The cookies have a nice sandy texture. They taste buttery. I found it to be a bit too sweet, but my husband did not. I tried few different jams but the raspberry definately comes out the best. Would only use raspberry next time. Did not use glaze as I did not want to open a whole can of evaporated milk just to use the tiny bit called for.

These were a huge hit with my family and my church. The ladies at my church recently had a cookie exchange in which I made these and I was told by several that their families thought these were the best. The only change I made was that I used Raspberry pie filling instead of raspberry jam. These are so easy to make and go quickly.

Yummy! I followed the recipe to the letter except that we didn't have raspberry jam so I substituted what we had... orange marmalade. Also, our oven is overly hot so I baked for 8 minutes, filled the cookies, and then finished off with another 5 minutes of baking. The cookies came out perfectly and the marmalade filling was delicious! The yield was 3 dozen and even though there's only my wife and myself here they're already half gone one hour later! Like I said... YUMMY! Thanks for sharing!
